questions.title: Collapse repeated delivery attempts
questions.prompt: Step 1 of 4. Implement collapseAttempts(attempts). Each attempt has a string deliveryId and string status. Return one new object with only deliveryId and status for each logical delivery. Return a fresh array. Keep the first attempt for a deliveryId and preserve the order in which distinct identifiers first appeared. Meet O(n) time and O(u) space for n attempts and u unique identifiers. Treat the input as read-only.
constraints: attempts contains zero or more plain JSON objects with string deliveryId and status fields.
Return one new { deliveryId, status } object for each distinct deliveryId.
Return a fresh result array that does not reuse the input array.
The first occurrence wins and distinct identifiers retain first-seen order.
A duplicate may be non-adjacent; comparing only neighboring records is not sufficient.
Expected complexity: O(n) time and O(u) space for u unique delivery identifiers.
Do not mutate the input array or its objects.

cases.label: rejects a non-adjacent duplicate without reordering

assertions.label: returns the first status for each identifier
keeps only the earliest x and y values

questions.title: Summarize an observation window
questions.prompt: Step 2 of 4. Implement summarizeWindow(events, startMs). Events are not guaranteed to be sorted. Include each event whose atMs is greater than or equal to startMs. Return a fresh { traffic, errors, maxLatencyMs } object, where errors counts events whose outcome is "error". Return zero for all fields when the window is empty. Meet O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space. Treat inputs as read-only.
constraints: Each event has finite numeric atMs and latencyMs fields plus a string outcome.
Input order is arbitrary and the start boundary is inclusive.
An old event may appear before a later in-window event, so early exit on timestamp is incorrect.
Expected complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space; do not sort.
Only the exact outcome string error increments errors.
Return a fresh summary object that does not reuse an input object.
Do not mutate the events array or its objects.

cases.label: keeps scanning after an old event in unsorted input

assertions.label: counts traffic errors and maximum latency

cases.label: returns zeros for an empty window
includes events exactly at the start

questions.title: Apply a per-tenant limit
questions.prompt: Step 3 of 4. Implement admitPerTenant(jobs, limit). Each job has string id and tenant fields. Walk jobs in arrival order and return a fresh array containing the ids of admitted jobs. Admit at most limit jobs for each tenant, while preserving the global order of every job that is admitted. A zero limit admits nothing. Meet O(n) time and O(t) space for n jobs and t tenants. Treat inputs as read-only.
constraints: jobs contains plain JSON objects with unique string id and string tenant fields.
limit is a non-negative integer applied independently to each tenant.
Return admitted job ids in their original global arrival order.
Return a fresh result array that does not reuse the jobs array.
Expected complexity: O(n) time and O(t) space for t distinct tenants.
Do not mutate the jobs array or its objects.

assertions.label: admits two jobs per tenant in arrival order

cases.label: admits nothing at a zero limit

assertions.label: admits the first job from each tenant
